studyArea.name: Seven Lakes of San Pablo City, Laguna
studyArea.assignmentLimit: The chapter discusses the seven-lake cluster collectively. It does not provide taxon-by-lake, station, or specimen assignments; these IDs define the study cluster only and are not occurrence links.

bibliography.title: Socio-economic and environmental impacts of COVID-19 pandemic: Building resilience of the seven lakes of San Pablo city, Philippines
bibliography.book: Environmental Resilience and Transformation in Times of COVID-19: Climate Change Effects on Environmental Functionality

method: Reviewed the chapter-specific JATS record through the official PMC OAI-PMH GetRecord endpoint and the indexed full-text sections on biodiversity, fish impacts, and aquaculture. The chapter is a secondary COVID-19 impact synthesis, not a new standardized fish survey. No image, table, raw paragraph, or supplementary fish dataset was retained.
sourceStatements: The chapter summarizes a collective 1940-1960 Seven Lakes fish-diversity list containing nine taxonomic labels: six binomial labels, one genus-level label, and two family-level labels. It provides no per-lake allocation or specimen/voucher crosswalk.

Its biodiversity prose says two native taxa remained present from 2001 onward while also naming additional native taxa as added to the list; the related Figure 23.6 caption bounds its photo labels to 2001-2020. These statements are internally unclear and do not provide a dated, lake-specific occurrence dataset.

The chapter attributes a pandemic-period increase of non-native red-devil and jaguar-guapote fish and predation on young tilapia/milkfish to a personal communication from the seven-lake FARMC. It reports no fish sampling, gut-content analysis, prey counts, sample dates, or lake-specific assignment. This is a predation research lead, not a species diet profile or bait recommendation.
The aquaculture section says tilapia cage culture began in Sampaloc Lake in 1976 and expanded to other San Pablo lakes later. This is culture history, not evidence of wild occurrence in each lake.

rights.copyright: The PMC JATS metadata states Copyright © 2021 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.
rights.permission: The article metadata includes Elsevier COVID-19 resource-center permission for unrestricted research re-use and analyses with acknowledgement while that resource center remains active. Elsevier’s current notice says COVID-19 material through July 2023 remains available for reading and text/data mining and that PMC may retain it under its original license.
rights.limits: Access through PMC does not itself grant unrestricted republication. No permission to reproduce its figure, images, tables, or chapter content in Bangwit was established; no app publication approval is granted.

limitations: No taxon is assigned to an individual lake, collection station, date, voucher, or sampling effort by this chapter.
The passage mixes historical descriptions, broad 2001-2020 photo context, and FARMC personal communication; it is not a consistent contemporary monitoring series.
The prose contains a native-fish status ambiguity and a mismatch between “2001 onward” and the figure caption’s 2001-2020 period.
Predation wording does not constitute a measured diet study and cannot be generalized into a species-wide natural diet card.
The chapter’s secondary *Carassius carassius* label does not resolve the Bunot carp conflict recorded in the separate 2017 survey review.
nextAction: Seek the underlying sources and lake-specific, rights-cleared fish surveys; resolve taxon-by-lake assignment and the Bunot carp identity before considering any species occurrence or diet projection.
